chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man gave a thousand dirhams to another man as a mudarabah (profit-sharing partnership), and he [the agent] bought a slave for him, while he [the agent] did not know [the value]. He [the Imam] said: 'It is appraised; if it exceeds by one dirham, he is freed, and he is given leeway in the man's wealth [to cover the difference].'

key_terms.أَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ: A thousand dirhams: The specific capital amount mentioned in the case.
key_terms.أُعْتِقَ: He is freed: The agent is released from liability for the excess value.
key_terms.اُسْتُسْعِيَ: Leeway is given: The agent is granted flexibility to cover the debt from the principal's assets.
key_terms.مُضَارَبَة: Mudarabah: A profit-sharing partnership in Islamic finance where one party provides capital and the other provides labor.
key_terms.يُقَوَّمُ: It is appraised: The process of determining the current market value of the purchased item.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if an agent buys a slave for a mudarabah partnership without knowing the price?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the risk-sharing mechanism in *mudarabah* (profit-sharing partnership) when an agent overpays for an asset. The ruling emphasizes fairness by requiring appraisal; if the value exceeds the principal by even a single dirham, the agent is exempt from covering that specific excess, reflecting the Shia principle that the investor bears the capital risk while the agent bears the labor risk, provided no negligence is proven.
